VIDEO TILE (Lantern 1.24.43) -- AN INDEPENDENT REVIEW BY A PERSON'S USE (REVIEW 2)
==================================================================================
Reviewer: a separate agent that did not write the tile. Date: 2026-11-26.
Build tested: site/index.html of branch lantern-1.24.43 (md5 53847e742d00e733d5751e1269b24110). src/ and site/ are the
same at commits 6600f22 and 128e0ff (only test files changed between them). Chromium (Playwright), headless,
1400 x 900 unless said; also 1366 x 768 and 390 x 844. Line numbers below are of src/lantern.inner.html.

Files here
  run.py       self-contained: makes its own media with ffmpeg in a temporary folder, serves ../../../site/index.html
               (or the build named as its first argument) and plays every scenario by mouse and keyboard: menus
               clicked, tools picked by their letters, clips clicked and dragged on the Timeline canvas, files chosen in
               the browser's file box, files dropped (a DataTransfer of real File objects), Project-panel and
               Source-Monitor drags (Playwright's HTML5 drag), values typed into Effect Controls, sliders dragged.
               Results are read from the app's state AND from what is shown or written: the Program and Source
               Monitor canvases, frames drawn by the renderer, the mixer's samples, and every exported file decoded by
               ffprobe/ffmpeg. One line per check, "PASS  ..." or "FAIL  ...  [what was seen]", then
               "<n> checks, <m> failed". Sections can be run alone: python3 run.py [build.html] [section ...]
               (start source tools keys edits trans fx graphics captions audio misc history play exportsec project
               menus views). A full run takes about 6.5 minutes on 2 cores.
  REPORT.txt   this file.

The media (made by run.py): a 320x240 30 fps H.264 clip with B-frames and AAC whose top row shows its own frame
number in binary (eight white boxes), with a white flash in its lower half at frames 45 and 120 and a 1 kHz beep on
exactly those frames over a quiet 200 Hz bed; the same design in VP9/Opus WebM (blue below), at 23.976 (72 frames,
red flash and beep at frame 24) and at 60 fps; a phone clip coded 1920x1080 with a 90-degree display rotation (red box
top-left of the upright picture, blue bottom-right); 1920x1080 at 29.97 with AAC; a mono WAV voice-over; MP3 and M4A
music; PNG and JPEG stills; a 90 s clip; a green-screen clip and a yellow background; a clip with hard cuts at frames
30 and 60; two recordings of the same claps 0.5 s apart; .srt and .vtt captions; an inverting .cube LUT.

How sure: "certain" = reproduced in the browser and traced to the code; "high" = reproduced, Premiere's behaviour well
known; "medium" = reproduced, but Premiere's exact behaviour is from memory and could differ in some version.

RESULT OF THE RUN: 549 checks, 54 failed (6 min 18 s). The run before it, identical but for one check corrected in
run.py, gave the same other 53 failures; the run before that the same again apart from two harness fixes. Every
failure below names its check (its text in run.py's output) in quotes; all 54 are covered by items 1-32.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT WORKS WELL (so the failures are read in proportion)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Frame accuracy is excellent: every Program frame tested (H.264 with B-frames, VP9, 23.976, a frame 60 s into a 90 s
  clip) is exactly the source frame; the Source Monitor steps exact frames; the phone clip is upright everywhere.
- Picture and sound stay in sync on import (AAC priming cut: beeps within 5 ms of the flash) and in every exported
  format: MP4 (H.264 + Opus), WebM VP9 and VP8, MOV (H.264 + PCM), AVI (MJPEG + PCM), WAV, the 23.976 export, the
  in-to-out export and the 50% export. Frame counts and durations match ffprobe to the frame.
- Export of GIF, PNG, JPEG, every-frame PNG zip and .srt work; Cancel works; -23 LUFS normalisation is within 0.5 LU of
  ffmpeg's ebur128; Measure loudness and true peak agree with ebur128.
- Insert, Overwrite and three-point editing from the Source Monitor, Lift, Extract, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+K, W, Delete,
  Ripple Delete, copy/paste/paste insert, Duplicate, slip, ripple edit, selection trims, Ctrl-drag insert, track
  changes, marquee, Track Select Forward, Hand, Zoom, mute/solo/eye, Nest's picture, Add Frame Hold, Speed/Duration
  (200%, reverse, duration typed), Close Gap, tracks added and removed.
- Undo and Redo put the tracks back exactly after every kind of edit tried (15 kinds); the History panel works.
- Transitions draw as their names say (Cross Dissolve mix checked against the formula; Dip to Black; fades to black and
  to silence at a clip's end). Effects, effect order, on/off, removal, keyframes (Linear, Hold, Ease), Lumetri (exactly
  neutral at its defaults; Saturation, Exposure, a .cube LUT), masks, Ultra Key (composite and alpha output), blend
  modes (Multiply and Screen checked against the formulas), adjustment layers, Paste Attributes.
- Essential Graphics (words, size, colour, background, position, layers), rolling credits off screen at both ends,
  crawl right to left; Captions import (.srt and .vtt), edit, export, show in Program and burn-in; Markers; the Audio
  Track Mixer (fader -6 dB halves the level exactly; pan; mute; master); Audio Gain (normalise to -1 dBFS exactly);
  Scopes; Scene Edit Detection (cuts or markers exactly at 30 and 60); Synchronize by sound (0.50 s found exactly).
- Playback runs at the sequence's rate (30, 23.976, 60) by the clock; J K L work; the Source Monitor plays.
- Save/Open Project round-trips exactly; reopening the last project and File > Link Media work; EDL out and in.
- No page errors in any section.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDINGS FIRST (edits that silently damage the work)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Q (Ripple Trim Previous Edit to Playhead) with V1 and A1 targeted -- the default -- moves everything after twice as
   far, laying clips over each other on the same track.
   Checks: "Q at 50 (Ripple Trim Previous Edit to Playhead): ..." and "after Q no two clips on a track lie over each other".
   Steps: two clips end to end (0-180 and 180-270, picture and sound); put the playhead at 50; press Q.
   What happens: the first clip becomes 0-130 (right), but the second moves to 80 instead of 130: V1 0-130 and 80-170
   overlap, the same on A1. The picture now shows a clip lying under another; the export follows the corrupted data.
   Expected: the second clip at 130 (Premiere moves the rest up by the 50 frames trimmed, once).
   Cause: C.trimTo (VIDEO_CMDS, ~65123) calls E.trimHead(..., "ripple") once per targeted track, and each call ripples
   every sync-locked track (VIDEO_EDIT trimHead, ~62303), so with two targeted tracks the shift is applied twice.
   (W happens to come out right only because the second track's clip no longer reaches the moved clips.) Sure: certain.

2. Speed/Duration with "Ripple Edit, Shifting Trailing Clips" on a clip with linked sound moves the following clips
   twice as far, leaving a gap.
   Check: "50% with Ripple Edit, Shifting Trailing Clips: ... (not twice as far)".
   Steps: select the first clip (0-180, its sound comes with it), Ctrl+R, 50%, tick Ripple, OK.
   What happens: the clip becomes 360 frames (right) but the next clip moves to 540 on V1 and A1, a 180-frame gap.
   Expected: the next clip at 360. Cause: the dialog calls E.setSpeed for the picture and for the sound (VIDEO_DIALOGS
   speed, ~66152) and each one ripples all sync-locked tracks (VIDEO_EDIT setSpeed, ~62366). Sure: certain.

3. Rolling Edit (N), Slide (U) and Rate Stretch (R) change the picture only; the linked sound stays where it was, so
   picture and sound drift apart with no warning.
   Checks: "Rolling Edit (N): the linked sound's cut moves with it ...", "Slide (U): the linked sound slides with the
   picture ...", "Rate Stretch (R): its linked sound is stretched to the same length and speed".
   Steps: one clip cut twice with the Razor (pieces 0-60, 60-120, 120-180); N, drag the cut at 60 to 80; or U, drag
   the middle piece 10 frames later; or R, drag the last clip's end 90 frames later.
   What happens: V1 changes as asked (checked: frame 79 shows source frame 79 after the roll); A1 is untouched (cuts
   still at 60/120; the stretched clip's sound still 180 frames at 100%). After a roll by 20 frames the sound of frames
   60-80 is the next piece's sound, 20 frames early. Premiere, with Linked Selection on, rolls, slides and stretches
   the linked audio with the video. Cause: the Timeline's apply() (VIDEO_TIMELINE, ~65574-65581) only edits the clip
   that was clicked for "roll", "rate" and "slide"; only plain/ripple trims and slip handle partners. Sure: certain.

4. Rate Stretch on a clip's head is wrong both ways: dragged left into the clip before, it lays the clip over it;
   with a gap before it and a clip after it, it cannot lengthen at all.
   Checks: "Rate Stretch (R) dragging a clip's head left never lays it over the clip before it on the track",
   "Rate Stretch (R): the head of a clip with a gap before it dragged 30 frames left makes it 90 frames at 66.7% ...".
   Steps: (a) three clips end to end; R; drag the head of the last clip (at 270) 30 frames left: it becomes 240-450 at
   85.7%, overlapping the clip 180-270 on V1. (b) delete the first piece (gap 0-60), R, drag the head of the piece at
   60 left 30 frames: nothing happens (the piece after it at 120 limits it).
   Cause: E.rateStretch limits the new length by the NEXT clip whatever edge is dragged, and nothing checks the clip
   before (VIDEO_EDIT ~62350; VIDEO_TIMELINE apply ~65575). Sure: certain.

5. A clip dragged to V2 (from the Project panel or the Source Monitor) puts its sound on A1, cutting into the sound of
   the clip already there, whose picture stays whole.
   Checks: "dragging a clip to V2 leaves the sound of the clip already on A1 whole (Premiere puts the new sound on A2,
   not over A1)" and "dragging a clip from the Source Monitor to V2 does not cut the sound of the clip on A1 under it
   (Premiere puts the sound on A2)".
   Steps: three clips end to end on V1/A1; drag counter_b.webm from the Project panel to V2 at frame 400.
   What happens: V2 400-490 (right) and its sound overwrites A1 400-490: clapA's sound (270-450) is cut to 270-400
   while its picture still runs to 450. From the Source Monitor's Drag handle to V2 at 200 the same: the sound of the
   clip on A1 at 180-270 is cut to 180-200. Expected (Premiere): the sound goes to the audio track that mirrors the video
   track (A2), never over another clip's sound unless dropped there. Cause: the drop handler sets only vTrack for a
   video row (VIDEO_TIMELINE ~65625) and C.addMedia then uses the targeted audio track (A1). Sure: certain.

6. Graphics > New Color Matte, New Bars and Tone and New Black Video overwrite five seconds of the clip on V1 at the
   playhead; a new graphic deletes what lies later on the track it picks.
   Checks: "Graphics > New Color Matte does not overwrite the clip on V1 under the playhead ...", "a new graphic made at
   0 does not cut or delete the title already on that track later (30-180)".
   Steps: (a) a clip on V1 0-180; playhead 60; Graphics > New Color Matte: V1 becomes 0-60 clip, 60-210 matte,
   210-270 the rest -- 150 frames of the edit replaced (and its picture gone; the sound stays). (b) a title on V2 at
   30-180; playhead 0; Graphics > New Rolling Credits: the credits go on V2 at 0-300 and the title is deleted.
   Expected: Premiere puts a new Color Matte, Bars and Tone or Black Video in the Project panel; a new graphic goes on a
   track that is free for its whole length (Premiere adds a track if it must). Nothing already in the edit is lost.
   Cause: C.newItem places on the targeted video track with E.place (VIDEO_CMDS ~65205), C.newGraphic picks the first
   track free AT the playhead only (~65198), and E.place clears what is under the new clip's whole length. Sure: certain.

7. Clips on a locked track are deleted by Select All (Ctrl+A) and Delete.
   Check: "Select All and Delete leave the clips on a locked track alone (Premiere cannot select them)".
   Steps: lock V1 (the padlock); Ctrl+A; Delete. Everything goes, the locked track's clips too.
   Expected: a locked track's clips cannot be selected or changed. (A click on them is refused, correctly.) Cause:
   C.selectAll selects every clip (VIDEO_CMDS ~65229), C.clear does not look at lock. Sure: certain.

8. A nested sequence clip is silent, and cannot be opened.
   Checks: "the nested clip keeps its sound ...", "double-clicking a nested clip opens its sequence in the Timeline".
   Steps: select both clips (picture and sound); Clip > Nest. The picture is right (frames 77 and 200 checked).
   What happens: the mix has no beeps at all: the sound of everything nested is gone, in playback and in export.
   Double-clicking the nested clip does nothing (Premiere opens the nested sequence). Cause: the mixer reads only clips
   with media (VIDEO_MIX clipSound, ~63860); the Timeline's dblclick handles only media clips and titles (~65614).
   Sure: certain.

9. Insert Frame Hold Segment pushes the picture two seconds later but not the sound.
   Check: "after Insert Frame Hold Segment the sound stays in sync with the picture ...".
   Steps: playhead 60 in the first clip; Clip > Insert Frame Hold Segment. The picture is right (hold of frame 60 at
   60-119, then frame 60 onward) but A1 is unchanged: from frame 120 the picture is 60 frames (2 s) behind the sound;
   the flash of source frame 120 is now at 180 and its beep still at 120. Expected: sync-locked tracks move with the
   insert (as every other insert in the tile does). Cause: E.shiftFrom on the video track only (VIDEO_CMDS ~65190).
   Sure: certain that sync is lost; medium on exactly how Premiere handles the linked audio (it does not leave it
   2 s out of sync).

10. Undo moves the playhead back to where it was at the earlier step.
   Check: "Undo does not move the playhead (Premiere leaves it where it is; it was at 200)".
   Steps: playhead 150, Ctrl+T (a title); playhead 200, Ctrl+K; Ctrl+Z: the playhead jumps to 150. Pressing Ctrl+Shift+K
   next (expecting a cut at 200) cuts at 150. Cause: each History step stores the whole project including
   seq.playhead (VIDEO_APP exec/go, ~64963-64981). Premiere's Undo does not move the playhead. Sure: high.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
OTHER FAILURES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Editing and the Timeline
11. "Insert with only V1 targeted: the picture goes in on V1, no sound; ..." -- with A1's target turned off (click A1
    in the header), Insert (,) still puts the sound in on A1. The help says Insert and Overwrite go "on the targeted
    tracks". Cause: tgt() falls back to the first unlocked track when none is targeted (VIDEO_CMDS ~65054). Sure: certain.
12. "dragging from the Source Monitor puts only the marked part (30 frames from 1.0 s), as Premiere does" -- the
    Drag handle under the Source Monitor puts the whole clip (90 frames from 0), not the marked In to Out. The dragstart
    stores text/x-lantern-src (VIDEO_MONITORS ~65289) but the Timeline's drop never reads it (~65622). Sure: certain.
13. "with snapping on, a clip dragged to within a frame of the playhead snaps its head to it (300)" -- a dragged clip's
    head does not snap to the playhead, markers or cuts unless its tail also lands near a snap point: the clip lands at
    299. In apply() (VIDEO_TIMELINE ~65569) the second snapF call (for the tail) resets st.snapAt to null, and then
    "if (st.snapAt === null) to = df" throws the head's snap away. Sure: certain.
14. "Alt-click on an already selected linked clip selects its picture alone (Premiere)" -- Alt-click picks one half only
    when the clip was not selected; on a selected pair it keeps both (selectClip, ~65545). Sure: certain.
15. "a click in a gap then Shift+Delete closes that gap ..." -- the status line says "select clips (or a gap) first",
    but a gap cannot be selected (a click there starts a marquee). Premiere selects a gap on a click and ripple-deletes
    it with Delete. Sure: certain.
16. "Sequence Settings: changing 30 to 25 fps on a sequence with clips is refused or keeps each clip's time in seconds
    (Premiere does not allow it)" -- the rate changes and every clip keeps its frame counts: a 6 s clip (180 frames)
    becomes 7.2 s, 1.2 s past the end of its media; nothing is said. Premiere greys out the timebase once a sequence
    exists. Sure: certain (behaviour); high (Premiere).

Transitions
17. "clicking the transition on the Timeline shows its settings ...", "with the transition clicked, Delete removes the
    transition and keeps both clips", "a transition's duration and alignment can be changed somewhere ..." -- a
    transition cannot be selected: a click on it selects the clip, and Delete then deletes the CLIP (both halves of the
    cut lose the second clip). There is no way to change a transition's duration, alignment or direction (Wipe, Push,
    Slide have From Left/Right/Top/Bottom settings that nothing in the UI reaches) or to remove one except Undo.
    Premiere: click selects the transition; Effect Controls shows Duration, Alignment and its settings; Delete removes
    it; its edges can be dragged. Sure: certain (behaviour).

Effects and sound
18. "Effects panel: Video Limiter (named in the help's list of video effects) is there" -- it is missing: VIDEO_FILT
    registers "limiter" (Video Limiter, ~63025) and VIDEO_AFX registers its Hard Limiter under the same id (~63674),
    which replaces it. Export's loudness limiter uses defs.limiter and so works only because the sound one won.
    Sure: certain.
19. "Amplify keyframed 0 dB at the clip's start to +12 dB at its end: the sound gets louder ..." -- Effect Controls
    offers the stopwatch on every sound effect's number, and keys are stored, but the mixer runs each effect with its
    values at frame 0 (VIDEO_MIX ~63878, F.values(e, 0)): the keyframes are ignored. Either honour them or do not show
    the stopwatch. (Clip Volume keyframes do work.) Sure: certain.
20. "Bars and Tone has its tone (Premiere's is a 1 kHz tone)" -- Bars and Tone is picture only; no tone is made.
    Sure: certain (behaviour); high (Premiere's Bars and Tone has a 1 kHz tone).
21. "the master meter moves while the sound plays" -- the meter beside the Timeline stays dark until the Audio Track
    Mixer tab has been opened once (then it works: "(once the Audio Track Mixer has been opened, the master meter does
    move)" passes). A.onMeter is defined only inside the mixer panel (VIDEO_PANELS ~65934). Also, from the code: each
    track's meter in the mixer is created but never drawn (only the master's is). Sure: certain.

Keys and menus
22. "Ctrl+Shift+M (Go to Previous Marker in the Markers menu) goes back to 45 and opens nothing" -- Ctrl+Shift+M opens
    Export Settings: the key handler's Ctrl branch tests "m" for Export before looking at Shift (VIDEO_MENUS ~66304).
    Sure: certain.
23. "Shift+5 ...", "Shift+6 ...", "Shift+7 ...", "Shift+2 ..." -- the Window menu shows Shift+5 (Effect Controls),
    Shift+6 (Audio Track Mixer), Shift+7 (Effects), Shift+2 (Source Monitor) as in Premiere, but the key handler
    explicitly ignores Shift with 2-7 (VIDEO_MENUS ~66329). Sure: certain.
24. Menu items that do nothing and say nothing when nothing is selected or the clipboard is empty (Premiere greys
    them out): Edit > Cut, Copy, Paste, Paste Insert, Paste Attributes, Clear, Duplicate; Clip > Enable, Scale to
    Frame Size, Fill Frame (checks "menu Edit > Cut (nothing selected; ...) does something or says why not ..." and the
    others). Other items do say why (Link, Nest, Speed/Duration, Audio Gain, Scene Edit Detection, Synchronize,
    Add Edit, Q/W, Lift/Extract, transitions). Sure: certain.
25. "turning a track's target on and off is not an Undo step (Premiere keeps History for edits)" -- every click on a
    track header button (target, sync lock, lock, eye, mute, solo) is a History step. After an edit and a few header
    clicks, Ctrl+Z first flips the header buttons back one by one before it reaches the edit, and the 100-step History
    fills with them. Premiere does not put these in History. Sure: high.
26. "after View > Safe Margins the Program Monitor's Safe button shows it is on" -- the menu turns the margins on but
    the Safe button under the Program Monitor stays unlit (its class is changed only by its own click, ~65285).
    Sure: certain.

Playing, monitors, timecode
27. "after New project from video files the playhead is at the start and the Program Monitor shows the first frame
    (not black past the end)" -- after bringing files in from the start screen the playhead sits after the last clip,
    so the first thing a beginner sees is a black Program Monitor (most visible on a phone). C.addMedia moves the
    playhead to the end of what it added (VIDEO_CMDS ~65085), which suits Insert/Overwrite but not a new project.
    Premiere's New Sequence from Clip leaves the playhead at the start. Sure: certain (behaviour); medium (Premiere).
28. "drop-frame timecode is written with semicolons throughout (00;01;00;02) as Premiere shows it" -- the tile shows
    00:01:00;02 (the frame count is right: drop-frame is computed correctly). Premiere displays drop-frame as
    00;01;00;02. Cosmetic. Sure: certain (tile); high (Premiere).

Export and exchange
29. "Export mp4: the status line says the sound is Opus because this browser cannot encode AAC" -- the note is written,
    then immediately replaced by "Saved Sequence 01.mp4 to Downloads" (VIDEO_DIALOGS ~66139 then VIDEO_APP download
    ~65028), so the person never learns the MP4 has Opus sound (which some televisions and old players do not play).
    The Export box does not say it beforehand either. Sure: certain.
30. "Export WAV with Loudness -16 LUFS of a mix with loud short beeps: ..." -- with short loud peaks in the mix the
    limiter pulls the result to -19.3 LUFS (ffmpeg ebur128), 3.3 LU short of the target, and the note still says the
    loudness was "brought to -16 LUFS". Loudness is not measured again after the limiter (VIDEO_EXPORT mixed, ~64600).
    The same export at -23 LUFS and a plain voice-over at -16 are both within 0.5 LU (pass). Either iterate (gain,
    limit, measure again) or say the target could not be reached. Sure: certain.
31. "Export Final Cut Pro XML: picture and sound are linked (<link> elements ...)" and "... the cross dissolve is in it
    (a <transitionitem>)" -- the XML has neither, so Premiere/Resolve get unlinked clips and no transitions. Sure:
    certain (file); high (Premiere writes and reads both).
32. "Import Final Cut Pro XML: the title comes back as a title, not as an offline clip over the picture" -- the title
    is written as a clip item without a file and comes back as a "Media offline" clip on V2 that covers the picture.
    (EDL import does the same, but says in the status line that "Graphic" was not found -- passing check; an EDL
    cannot carry a title, so that is expected there.) Sure: certain.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
OBSERVATIONS (not pass/fail)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Default scaling: new clips get "Set to Frame Size" (the project preference scaling: "set"). Premiere's default
  Default Media Scaling is None (a large clip shows at 100%, cropped). Lantern's choice is friendlier; it differs.
- Playback resolution defaults to 1/2 even for a 320x240 sequence, so a small sequence looks soft in the Program
  Monitor (see the counter's boxes). Premiere chooses by the frame size; 1/2 for SD is not its default.
- The tools are symbols only (the letter is only in the tooltip); the track header buttons are symbols too. A
  beginner on a phone (no tooltips) cannot tell Rolling from Ripple or Slip from Slide.
- The Export box shows "GIF width", "Audio bitrate" and "Burn in captions" for every format (e.g. GIF width for MP4,
  audio bitrate for a GIF). Showing only what the chosen format uses would be clearer.
- The project is always called "Untitled": Save Project downloads Untitled.lvproj, and opening "My film.lvproj" keeps
  the name Untitled. There is no way to name the project.
- Paste puts clips back on the tracks they were copied from. Premiere pastes on the targeted tracks (the lowest
  targeted video and audio track). Sure: medium.
- Paste Attributes pastes everything (Motion, Opacity, every effect, keyframes, volume) at once; Premiere asks which
  attributes in a dialog.
- Ctrl+K with a clip selected on an untargeted track cuts that track as well as the targeted ones. Premiere, when
  clips are selected, cuts only the selected clips. Sure: medium.
- End puts the playhead on the last frame (269 of 270); Premiere puts it just after (270). The check accepts both.
- Import EDL: the picture and sound events come back unlinked.
- Import into the start screen's "New project from video files" sets the status to the sequence-settings note,
  which is useful; "Imported 2 of 2" is replaced at once.
- The Captions panel's "Show in Program" is changed on the sequence without an Undo step and is saved only with the
  next edit (if the page is closed right after ticking it, it is not kept).
- Phone (390 x 844): everything fits the width (checks pass), but the Program Monitor takes 42% of the height above
  the panels, the Timeline is far below, and the Snap/Linked/Fit buttons crowd the timecode box. Laptop (1366 x 768):
  fits without page scroll; only V3-A2 rows of the Timeline show (A3 needs scrolling).
- Status line: most edits that cannot be done say why (good); edits that succeed say nothing, which is fine.
- From reading the code only (not run): the Audio Track Mixer's per-track meters are created but never drawn.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTES ON THE CHECKS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Descriptions are fixed text; what was seen follows in brackets. The check list is deterministic: the same failures
  came out in two full runs. A failure in one section does not stop the others (each section opens its own page).
- Where a check depends on Premiere's behaviour rather than the tile's own help, the check's text says "(Premiere)" or
  "as Premiere does", and the certainty is given above.
- The menu sweep (section menus) runs every item from a state with nothing selected, in and out at 30 and 59, markers
  at 45 and 150, the playhead at 100; an item passes if it opens a dialog or a file box, downloads, changes the
  project, the view, the tool or the panel, or writes to the status line, with no page error.
